earlier_versions_unchanged: results/results-r1.json, results/results-heldout.json, results/results-r2.json and results/results-r2-breakdown.json stay as scored

measures.a: one-fit rule: each county bank debit's check number treated as unreadable in turn; close only when exactly one open payment within US$1.00 issued 0 to W business days before fits; two or more go to a person; wrong closes per 1,000 debits over all debits
measures.b: by payment type: the version 2 forced pick (wrong per 1,000 debits within reach) and the one-fit rule (wrong closes per 1,000 debits), paper and electronic separately
measures.c: exact cents first: the version 2 forced pick preferring payments equal to the debit to the cent, then the oldest, then the lowest id

predictions.claim: one-fit wrong closes at or above 1 per 1,000 debits at 5, 10 and 15 business days
predictions.opposite: under 1 per 1,000 at any of them

predictions.claim: at 60 business days one-fit wrong closes under 1 per 1,000 debits
at 5 business days look-alikes are 25% to 45% of debits within reach, and a larger share at 60 than at 5
at 5 business days the one-fit rule closes right 35% to 55% of all debits
at 5 business days the forced pick's wrong rate within reach is higher for paper than for electronic debits
predictions.opposite: as high or higher for electronic

predictions.claim: at 5 business days exact-cents-first wrong picks within reach are 1,121 to 1,200

call_rule.some_window_under_1_per_1000: close alone only when one payment fits, at the narrowest such window; send look-alikes to a person
call_rule.statement_test: count wrong closes over all debits; zero in at least 3,000 debits puts the 95% upper bound under 1 per 1,000
